title: Isolation and characterization of circulating pro-vascular progenitor cell subsets from human whole blood samples
protocol: Place up to 25 mL of collected whole blood in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Dilute blood sample 1:1 with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and mix thoroughly.
Fill 15 mL SepMate tube with 4 mL of room temperature Ficoll Paque.
Insert serological pipette tip into the SepMate insert groove to guide the addition of Ficoll.
Layer up to 10 mL of whole blood + PBS solution into the SepMate collection tubes.
Use the slowest setting on the pipette controller to gently layer the mixture onto the Ficoll.
Hold the SepMate tube at a slight angle while layering the blood.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,500 rpm (approximately 425 × g) for 10 min at room temperature with the brake ON.
If unable to use SepMate system, centrifuge for 20 min without brake.
Ensure proper balance of the centrifuge during processing.
Remove the sample from the centrifuge and collect the fluid above the SepMate insert in a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube.
Pour over contents directly if using SepMate; avoid debris and red blood cells contamination.
Use a transfer pipette for removal of buffy coat without disturbing the red blood cell pellet if not using SepMate.
Discard used SepMate tubes to maintain a clean workspace.
Dilute the mononuclear cell sample 1:1 with PBS + 5% FBS.
Centrifuge the diluted sample at 1,500 rpm for 7 minutes with break ON.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of PBS + 5% FBS.
Add 9 mL of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) red cell lysis buffer to the suspension.
Let the sample rest at room temperature for 8 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample again at 1,500 rpm for 7 minutes with break ON.
Remove the supernatant if pink or red coloring remains in the pellet.
Repeat steps 8–10 up to two additional times to maximize erythrocyte depletion.
Resuspend the final cell pellet by washing with 3 mL of Aldefluor buffer assay solution.
If the pellet does not dissolve completely, add more Aldefluor Assay Buffer to ensure proper emulsion.
Pipette approximately 20 μL of mixed sample into a 0.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 20 μL of Trypan blue to the Eppendorf tube and mix thoroughly.
Add 10 μL of the cell solution + trypan mixture to each hemocytometer chamber.
Count the viable (clear) and non-viable cells in the hemocytometer chambers.
Adjust the sample concentration to 1 × 10^6 cells/mL with Aldefluor Assay Buffer.
Label 5 mL polystyrene Falcon tubes according to various surface markers and controls.
Label one tube "no-ALDH."
Label one tube "ALDH-inhibited."
Label one tube "ALDH-stained."
Allow the Aldefluor reagent and kit components to come to room temperature (20°C).
Remove an aliquot of previously activated Aldefluor substrate from the freezer (−20°C) and allow it to come to room temperature (20°C).
Place 1 mL of cell solution into a tube labeled "no-ALDH."
Cap the tube labeled "no-ALDH" and set it aside.
Place 2 mL of cell solution into an additional tube labeled "ALDH-stained."
Add 5 μL of Aldefluor DEAB Reagent to the "ALDH-inhibited" (DEAB) tube.
Recap the DEAB vial immediately after use.
Mix 5 μL of activated Aldefluor Reagent per mL of sample in the "ALDH-stained" tube.
Transfer 500 μL of cell mixture from the "ALDH-stained" tube to the "ALDH-inhibited" (DEAB) tube.
Gently mix the "ALDH-inhibited" and "ALDH-stained" samples with a P1000 pipette.
Incubate both "ALDH-inhibited" and "ALDH-stained" samples at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 30–60 min.
Keep the "no-ALDH" tube at 2°C–8°C until the other samples are removed from the incubator.
Label a 5 mL polystyrene Falcon tube according to each fluorochrome being examined.
Add an equal sample volume from the "no-ALDH" unstained control into each fluorochrome labeled tube.
Incubate the "ALDH-inhibited" and "ALDH-stained" tubes for 30–60 min in the incubator.
Remove the "ALDH-inhibited" and "ALDH-stained" tubes from the incubator after incubation.
Mix the contents of each tube with a P1000 pipette.
Allocate an equal sample volume from the "ALDH-stained" sample tube into each fluorescence minus one (FMO) control tube.
Allocate an equal sample volume from the "ALDH-stained" sample tube into each fully stained panel tube.
Store any remaining sample in the "ALDH-stained" control.
Centrifuge FMO tubes, full panel tubes, “ALDH-inhibited” and “ALDH-stained” control tubes at 1,500 rpm for 5 minutes with the break ON.
Remove supernatant from each tube described in step 26.
Resuspend the pellet in approximately 200 μL of Aldefluor Assay Buffer per sample tube using a P200 pipette.
Add 4 μL of each antibody to your test tube based on specified panels using a P10 or P20 micropipette.
Mix gently with a P200 pipette to ensure proper mixture of the sample.
Change pipette tips when introducing each unique antibody to avoid contamination.
Place only the fluorochrome of interest in each fluorochrome isotype tube.
For FMO tubes, place every fluorochrome except the one of interest.
For full panel tubes, place all antibodies specific to each cell panel.
Place all samples in the fridge at 2°–8°C for at least 30 minutes.
Allow for appropriate antibody binding onto MNCs.
Incubate samples.
Place all samples, including "non-ALDH" unstained control, in the centrifuge at 1,500 rpm (approximately 425 × g) for 5 minutes with the break ON.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in approximately 300 μL of Aldefluor Assay Buffer using a P1000 pipette.
Ensure that the pellet is properly dissolved in the solution.
If the solution appears cloudy, add more Aldefluor Assay Buffer until the sample is clear.
Cap the 5 mL polystyrene Falcon tubes.
Place the tubes in the fridge (2°C–8°C) until ready to be analyzed on the flow cytometer.
Ensure that cells are analyzed within 3 hours if not immediately analyzed or within 24 hours of peripheral blood collection.
Prepare unstained control sample.
Record 50,000 events for unstained control sample.
Gate on cellular events based on forward and side scatter values.
Remove debris and red blood cell contamination from analysis.
Create compensation tubes specific for each fluorochrome.
Record 20,000 events per compensation tube.
Prepare DEAB control to establish positive and negative regions for ALDH activity.
Set gate at < 0.5% for DEAB inhibition.
Record 50,000 events for DEAB control sample.
Record 50,000 events for ALDH activity assessment in PBMNCs.
Establish gates for each fluorochrome using fluorescence minus one (FMO) tubes.
Prepare full panel analyses with all surface marker antibodies in the specific testing panel.
Record upwards of 1 million events for rare cellular event examination.
